Claude loads either tool when it needs it, and if one appears only as a deferred tool's name, Claude loads it the way this session loads deferred tools before calling it.

**Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

edits.description: publish: small changes Claude makes to the file at `file_path` in this same call, instead of editing the file with Edit and publishing after. Use it on a page (add `url` to update an artifact from another conversation) or on one data file of an artifact made from a type (its `url`, with that file as `file_path`). Not allowed with `type_url` or `files`. Each old_str is text copied exactly from the file as it now stands and must occur in it exactly once; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it). The edits apply in order, all or none: the file is published with them and then saved with them on disk, so it stays the source for later changes; on a miss nothing is changed or published, and the result says which edit failed and why.

old_str.description: Text copied exactly from the file; must occur once.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes the published path of a `files` entry. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` is served at its path relative to `root`, unless a `files` map entry states its served path. Claude sends it with every such publish, set to the folder that holds the Artifact's files at their served paths.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a dashboard that shows data, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

138	Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.
139	Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)
140	Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
141	Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
142	Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.

144	Allocation
145	
146	When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.

148	The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.

160	The tenant clicks Pay now on their lease. Your API creates a gateway bill for the amount due now: the unpaid amounts of the lease's invoices due on or before today's Malaysia date. If nothing is due, refuse. Bill ids must be impossible to guess.
161	In production the tenant would now be redirected to the gateway. In this test, show the bill id and amount: we play the gateway using the simulator below.
162	The gateway calls your webhook, POST /api/webhooks/gateway. Only the webhook can settle a bill. The gateway also sends the tenant back to /payments/return?bill_id=...&paid=true. That page only shows the bill's real status from your database and changes nothing.
163	Webhook
164	
165	The request body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with these fields. The gateway may add more fields in future.
166	
167	FIELD EXAMPLE NOTES
168	id bill_8f3a2c Your bill id (this short example is guessable; yours must not be)
169	paid true true or false
170	paid_amount 210050 Amount in sen; 0 when not paid
171	paid_at 2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800 When it was paid
172	transaction_id TX-000123 Gateway transaction id
173	transaction_status completed completed, failed or pending
174	x_signature 06994f... See below
175	
176	Signature. Take every field in the request except x_signature, sort them by key (ascending by character code), write each one as the key immediately followed by the value, join them with |, and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the resulting string with your secret key GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY, as lowercase hex. Test vector, with the key test_x_signature_key and the six example values above:
177	
178	source: idbill_8f3a2c|paidtrue|paid_amount210050|paid_at2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800|transaction_idTX-000123|transaction_statuscompleted
179	signature: 06994fab2d674e7829144eaa2204631716d3c099b503d38945e92b6296531641
180	
181	Required behavior:
182	
183	SITUATION RESPONSE EFFECT
184	Signature missing or wrong 401 None
185	Unknown bill id 404 None
186	paid=true and paid_amount is not the bill's amount 422 None
187	paid=true, bill pending or failed 200 Bill becomes paid, and one approved online payment is created with received_at = paid_at, then allocated
188	paid=true, bill already paid (a repeat delivery) 200 None
189	paid=false, bill pending 200 Bill becomes failed
190	paid=false, bill already failed (a repeat delivery) 200 None
191	paid=false, bill already paid (late or out of order) 200 None: a paid bill never goes back
192	
193	The gateway retries, so it may deliver the same callback several times, including at the same moment. A bill creates at most one payment, ever. Never log the secret key or whole callback payloads.

223	6. Access Control
224	
225	Access is enforced in two places, and we test both:
226	
227	Your server code: route handlers, Server Actions and server components. Every endpoint must authenticate the caller and check their organization and role itself. A protected page or a hidden button is not a check.
228	The Supabase Data API and Storage, which anyone holding your publishable key can call directly with their own access token.
229	Server code
230	Roles come from your memberships table, and from tenants.user_id for tenants. Never take a role or an organization from anything the user can edit, such as user_metadata.
231	On the server, authenticate with supabase.auth.getUser() or getClaims(), not getSession().
232	A request about a record in another organization, or another tenant's record, gets 404: do not reveal that it exists. A request about a record the caller can see, for an action their role does not allow, gets 403. A request without a valid login gets 401.
233	IDs in request bodies are untrusted too. For example, a manager must not be able to create a lease on another organization's unit or tenant.
234	Our tests call your API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, where the token is a Supabase access token for one of the seeded users. Accept that header as well as the normal session cookie.
235	The service role (secret) key must never reach the browser.
236	Data API
237	
238	This table is the most access allowed through the Supabase Data API, which is PostgREST called with a user's token. Granting less is fine where your app does not need it, with one exception: the tenant portal reads the tenant's own data, and updates their phone number, directly from the browser with supabase-js.

125	## Error contract (brief overrides the kit default)
126	- Body on error: `{ "error": "message" }` (R45) — a plain string. Rejected: kit's `{error:{code,message}}` (the brief fixes the shape).
127	- Check order in every handler: 401 (no/invalid token) → load the target record; not visible to the caller (other org, other tenant, nonexistent, malformed uuid) → 404 → role not allowed on a visible record (or no-record endpoint like POST /api/leases, reports) → 403 → body validation 400 → business rules 409 / 422.
128	- 400: malformed JSON, unknown keys (zod `.strict()`), bad types, invalid dates, invalid range. 409: overlap (23P01), not pending / not approved, idempotency key reused with a different payload. 422: over cap / over remaining balance / nothing due / webhook amount mismatch. 500: generic `{ "error": "Internal error" }`, no SQL, no stack.
129	- private.* plpgsql raises fixed SQLSTATEs: `P0409` conflict, `P0422` business rule, `P0404` not found, `P0400` validation; `src/lib/errors.ts` maps them + 23P01/23505 → 409, 22P02/P2023 → 400, P2025 → 404, 40001/40P01 → one retry then 409.

131	## Domain rules (PROPOSED unless marked "brief")
132	- Money: bigint sen in SQL (brief R48), `number` in TS; Prisma BigInt converted to number in ONE helper (`toSen`) that throws if not a safe integer; never floats. Single currency MYR: `currency char(3) not null default 'MYR' check (currency = 'MYR')` on leases/invoices/payments/gateway_bills (kit rule). Rejected: no currency column (kit asks for a CHECK when one currency).
133	- Rounding: half up, only for proration (non-negative), integer arithmetic `floor((2·rent·used + full) / (2·full))`, in ONE function `roundHalfUpDiv` inside `src/lib/billing.ts` (billing.ts must be self-contained: brief tests it directly, so it imports nothing). `src/lib/money.ts` re-exports it + `parseRinggitToSen` and adds `formatSen`. Rejected: rounding in money.ts imported by billing.ts (a grader copying/importing billing.ts alone must work; also one less module to explain).
134	- Dates (brief R3/R17): calendar dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings; month math on {y,m,d} via `Date.UTC`, never local getters. "Today in Malaysia" = `toMytDate(now)` = `new Date(now.getTime() + 8h).toISOString().slice(0,10)` (Malaysia has no DST; fixed +08:00). SQL twin: `(p_as_of at time zone 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur')::date`. Rejected: Intl.DateTimeFormat (works too, but more surface; fixed offset is exact for MYT).
135	- Instants in the API: input `receivedAt` must be ISO 8601 WITH an offset or `Z` (else 400 — ambiguous); output instants formatted in MYT with offset, e.g. `2026-01-31T10:00:00+08:00`. Rejected: accepting naive strings as MYT (silent assumptions; the brief says instants carry an offset).
136	- Billing period = anchor-to-anchor (brief R13/R14); proration only on the last period (brief R15); start==end → one 1-day period prorated over the full period length.
137	- Late fee: none in Part A (only in the Part B review code) → not built.
138	- Payments: partial allowed; manual over cap → 422 (brief R22); online payments are never refused once captured — leftover → unapplied_sen (brief R26). Allocation order brief R26.
139	- Cap formula (R22): `cap = Σ invoices.amount_sen − Σ allocations.amount_sen (of non-voided payments) − Σ payments.amount_sen where status = pending_verification`; request must be `0 < amountSen ≤ cap`. Approve re-check (R23): `amount ≤ Σ invoices − Σ allocations` (pending ones excluded, per the brief's wording).
140	- Void (R24): deletes that payment's allocation rows, sets status voided, keeps the payment row; unapplied_sen of OTHER payments is not re-applied (brief: "Other payments' allocations do not change") — see Q3.
141	- Payments are never deleted (R25): a `private` trigger blocks DELETE and allows UPDATE only for the transitions pending_verification→approved/rejected, approved→voided (plus unapplied_sen/allocation bookkeeping inside the private functions); amount, method, received_at, lease, org are immutable. Rejected: kit's "refunds/voids are new rows" (the brief changes status on the same row).
142	- Overdue grace = 0 days (brief R17: overdue the day after dueDate). The 7-day grace exists only in the Part B review code.
143	- Invoice status: never stored (brief R27). Server computes with `invoiceStatus(…, asOf)` from billing.ts; dashboard overdue count also via invoiceStatus. No SQL status twin needed.
144	- Concurrency (R28/R35/R46): every money write locks the **lease row** `FOR UPDATE` first (cap and allocation are lease-wide), then the payment / bill row; webhook locks the bill row first then the lease (always bill → lease order; other paths never lock bills). Lease overlap: `EXCLUDE USING gist (unit_id WITH =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') WITH &&)` (btree_gist). One payment per bill: partial `UNIQUE (gateway_bill_id)` on payments + bill status check under the lock. Rejected: SERIALIZABLE + retries (more 409s under load, harder to explain); advisory locks (invisible in schema).
145	- Money writes live in plpgsql functions in schema `private` called by server code via Prisma `$queryRaw` (owner role): `private.record_payment`, `private.approve_payment`, `private.reject_payment`, `private.void_payment`, `private.allocate_payment` (internal), `private.create_gateway_bill`, `private.apply_gateway_callback`. Lease creation = Prisma interactive transaction (lease + createMany(invoices from generateSchedule) + audit row). Each private function: revoke from public; no grant to anon/authenticated.
146	- Idempotency for manual payments: brief's body has no key → optional `Idempotency-Key` header (uuid); when present, UNIQUE (org_id, idempotency_key): same payload → original `{id,status}` 200, different payload → 409. Never required (see Q1). Webhook idempotency = bill state machine under `FOR UPDATE` + unique gateway_bill_id (no 5-minute replay window: brief has no timestamp field and the gateway retries).
147	- Webhook parsing: raw body `await req.text()` → `URLSearchParams`; duplicate keys → 400; signature over all fields except x_signature (extra fields included, R32); `timingSafeEqual` on equal-length hex buffers; 401 before anything else. Bill id that is not a uuid → 404. paid_at must match `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS ±HHMM` → converted to timestamptz; paid_amount must be `^\d+$`. Logged: bill id + outcome only. Bill outcome follows the `paid` flag only (R34); transaction_status is stored but does not drive the state machine. Bill amount compared against the bill's stored amount_sen, not a recalculated due amount. Amount due for a bill ignores pending manual payments (brief R30 wording).

101	Validation. Throw an Error if a date is not a real calendar date written as YYYY-MM-DD, if endDate is before startDate, if monthlyRentSen is not a positive integer, or if depositSen is not a non-negative integer.
102	Deposit. If depositSen > 0, the first invoice is the deposit: kind: 'deposit', due on startDate, period fields null.
103	Anchors. Rent periods are anchored on the start date. The anchor of period k is the start date plus k calendar months, always counted from the start date (never from the previous anchor). If that month has fewer days than the start day, use the month's last day. A lease starting on Jan 31 has anchors Jan 31, Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31, Apr 30, and so on.
104	Periods. Period k runs from anchor k to the day before anchor k+1, and is due on anchor k. There is a period for every anchor on or before endDate.
105	Last period. It is cut at endDate. If it is shorter than its full length, it costs monthlyRentSen x days used / days in the full period, rounded half up to the nearest sen. Every other period costs monthlyRentSen.
106	Order. The deposit first, then rent by period index.

133	4. Payments
134	Recording a payment
135	Staff and managers record cash or bank transfer payments on a lease: the amount, the method, and the date and time the money was received (entered and shown in Malaysia time).
136	A bank transfer needs a slip: a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB, stored in Supabase Storage (section 6). If recording fails after the upload, the file must not be left behind.
137	A payment recorded by a manager is approved immediately. A payment recorded by staff is pending_verification until a manager approves or rejects it.
138	Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.
139	Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)
140	Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
141	Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
142	Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.
143	Payments are never deleted. Every approval, rejection, void and lease creation writes a row to audit_log (who, what, when, details).
144	Allocation
145	
146	When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.
147	
148	The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.
149	
150	All of this must stay correct when requests arrive at the same time. For example, two staff members recording payments on the same lease at once must not exceed the cap together, and a payment approved twice at once is allocated once.
151	
152	Collections report
153	
154	The total of approved payments for each calendar month of received_at in Malaysia time, over a range of months, including months with nothing collected. With the seed data, Northwind's report for 2026-01 to 2026-03 is [{ month: '2026-01', collectedSen: 300000 }, { month: '2026-02', collectedSen: 0 }, { month: '2026-03', collectedSen: 200000 }].

126	- Body on error: `{ "error": "message" }` (R45) — a plain string. Rejected: kit's `{error:{code,message}}` (the brief fixes the shape).
127	- Check order in every handler: 401 (no/invalid token) → load the target record; not visible to the caller (other org, other tenant, nonexistent, malformed uuid) → 404 → role not allowed on a visible record (or no-record endpoint like POST /api/leases, reports) → 403 → body validation 400 → business rules 409 / 422.

131	## Domain rules (PROPOSED unless marked "brief")
132	- Money: bigint sen in SQL (brief R48), `number` in TS; Prisma BigInt converted to number in ONE helper (`toSen`) that throws if not a safe integer; never floats. Single currency MYR: `currency char(3) not null default 'MYR' check (currency = 'MYR')` on leases/invoices/payments/gateway_bills (kit rule). Rejected: no currency column (kit asks for a CHECK when one currency).
133	- Rounding: half up, only for proration (non-negative), integer arithmetic `floor((2·rent·used + full) / (2·full))`, in ONE function `roundHalfUpDiv` inside `src/lib/billing.ts` (billing.ts must be self-contained: brief tests it directly, so it imports nothing). `src/lib/money.ts` re-exports it + `parseRinggitToSen` and adds `formatSen`. Rejected: rounding in money.ts imported by billing.ts (a grader copying/importing billing.ts alone must work; also one less module to explain).
134	- Dates (brief R3/R17): calendar dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings; month math on {y,m,d} via `Date.UTC`, never local getters. "Today in Malaysia" = `toMytDate(now)` = `new Date(now.getTime() + 8h).toISOString().slice(0,10)` (Malaysia has no DST; fixed +08:00). SQL twin: `(p_as_of at time zone 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur')::date`. Rejected: Intl.DateTimeFormat (works too, but more surface; fixed offset is exact for MYT).
135	- Instants in the API: input `receivedAt` must be ISO 8601 WITH an offset or `Z` (else 400 — ambiguous); output instants formatted in MYT with offset, e.g. `2026-01-31T10:00:00+08:00`. Rejected: accepting naive strings as MYT (silent assumptions; the brief says instants carry an offset).
136	- Billing period = anchor-to-anchor (brief R13/R14); proration only on the last period (brief R15); start==end → one 1-day period prorated over the full period length.
137	- Late fee: none in Part A (only in the Part B review code) → not built.
138	- Payments: partial allowed; manual over cap → 422 (brief R22); online payments are never refused once captured — leftover → unapplied_sen (brief R26). Allocation order brief R26.
139	- Cap formula (R22): `cap = Σ invoices.amount_sen − Σ allocations.amount_sen (of non-voided payments) − Σ payments.amount_sen where status = pending_verification`; request must be `0 < amountSen ≤ cap`. Approve re-check (R23): `amount ≤ Σ invoices − Σ allocations` (pending ones excluded, per the brief's wording).
140	- Void (R24): deletes that payment's allocation rows, sets status voided, keeps the payment row; unapplied_sen of OTHER payments is not re-applied (brief: "Other payments' allocations do not change") — see Q3.
141	- Payments are never deleted (R25): a `private` trigger blocks DELETE and allows UPDATE only for the transitions pending_verification→approved/rejected, approved→voided (plus unapplied_sen/allocation bookkeeping inside the private functions); amount, method, received_at, lease, org are immutable. Rejected: kit's "refunds/voids are new rows" (the brief changes status on the same row).
142	- Overdue grace = 0 days (brief R17: overdue the day after dueDate). The 7-day grace exists only in the Part B review code.
143	- Invoice status: never stored (brief R27). Server computes with `invoiceStatus(…, asOf)` from billing.ts; dashboard overdue count also via invoiceStatus. No SQL status twin needed.
144	- Concurrency (R28/R35/R46): every money write locks the **lease row** `FOR UPDATE` first (cap and allocation are lease-wide), then the payment / bill row; webhook locks the bill row first then the lease (always bill → lease order; other paths never lock bills). Lease overlap: `EXCLUDE USING gist (unit_id WITH =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') WITH &&)` (btree_gist). One payment per bill: partial `UNIQUE (gateway_bill_id)` on payments + bill status check under the lock. Rejected: SERIALIZABLE + retries (more 409s under load, harder to explain); advisory locks (invisible in schema).
145	- Money writes live in plpgsql functions in schema `private` called by server code via Prisma `$queryRaw` (owner role): `private.record_payment`, `private.approve_payment`, `private.reject_payment`, `private.void_payment`, `private.allocate_payment` (internal), `private.create_gateway_bill`, `private.apply_gateway_callback`. The second request blocks on that lock until the first commits. Only then does it compute the cap (lines 186-188), and the cap now subtracts the first RM 800, which is pending_verification, so only RM 200 is left and the RM 700 gets 422. # Test helpers (owned by test-engineer; signatures are stable, ask the lead before changing one)

Run anything that touches the DB as `bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run <path>` from `./app`.
Env comes from `.env.local` (then `.env`) via `vitest.config.mts`. `tests/setup/global.ts` points
`TEST_BASE_URL` at a live Next server (3000, else it starts `next dev -p 3100` and stops it after).
Test files run one at a time (`fileParallelism: false`); tests inside a file are sequential unless you use `Promise.all`.

| module | export | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `env.ts` | `env.supabaseUrl / publishableKey / secretKey / databaseUrl / gatewayKey / seedPassword / baseUrl` | typed, lazy env getters (throw if missing) |
| `clients.ts` | `anonClient()` | supabase-js with the publishable key, no user |
| | `userClient(accessToken)` | publishable key + `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (PostgREST, RPC, Storage as that user) |
| | `adminClient()` | secret key (setup only: auth admin, storage cleanup) |
| `db.ts` | `pool()`, `sql<T>(text, params)` | pg pool on DATABASE_URL as `postgres` (bypasses RLS). int8 -> number (throws if unsafe), date -> `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string. Call `closePool()` in `afterAll` |
| | `newConnection(): Promise<pg.Client>` | a separate connected session for race tests; `await c.end()` yourself |
| `seeded.ts` | `SEEDED` | key -> email of the 7 brief accounts: `northwindManager, northwindStaff, aisyah, ben, probe, betaManager, chen` |
| | `signIn(email, password = SEED_PASSWORD, { fresh? }) -> { userId, email, accessToken }` | real password grant; cached in memory + `node_modules/.cache` while the token has >10 min left and its auth.sessions row still exists. `fresh: true` for a test that signs out |
| | `seeded(key)`, `ctxFor(key) -> { userId }` | sign in a seeded account / ctx for calling services directly |
| `http.ts` | `api(token?)` -> `{ get(path), post(path, body?), request(method, path, body?) }` | route handlers over HTTP with `Authorization: Bearer`, `redirect: 'manual'`; returns `{ status, body, headers }` (body = parsed JSON, else text). A string body is sent verbatim. `opts.headers` adds headers (e.g. `Idempotency-Key`) |
| | `postForm(path, fields | pairs)` | x-www-form-urlencoded POST, no auth (webhook) |
| `gateway.ts` | `gatewaySignature(fields, key?)`, `gatewayPaidAt(date)`, `signedCallback(billId, amountSen, paid, extra?, key?)` | brief §5 signature written independently of the app |
| `fixtures.ts` | `createFixtureOrg({ name?, units = 2, lease?, leaseTenant = 'A' }) -> FixtureOrg` | fresh org: manager + staff memberships, units, tenants A/B linked to fresh auth users (`*@fixture.test`, SEED_PASSWORD, signed in). `lease` inserts a lease on `unitIds[0]` + exactly `generateSchedule(lease)` invoices. Returns `{ orgId, orgName, unitIds, tenantAId, tenantBId, users: {manager, staff, tenantA, tenantB}, tokens: {...}, lease?: { id, ..., invoices: [{ id, ...ScheduledInvoice }] } }` |
| | `insertLease(orgId, unitId, tenantId, lease, createdBy?)`, `insertUnit(orgId, name?)`, `insertTenant(orgId, userId, fullName, email)`, `createFixtureUser(label)` | building blocks (direct pg, no audit rows) |
| `time.ts` | `asOf(isoWithOffset)`, `mytAt(date, "HH:MM[:SS]")`, `mytMidnight(date)`, `mytEndOfDay(date)` | deterministic instants; `asOf` rejects naive strings |

Fixtures are never deleted (D29: payments and audit_log are append-only); use random names.
Never insert payments/allocations directly to set up a scenario you then assert on: go through the API or the
`private.*` functions so the rows are the ones the app would produce.

Success logs console.info('gateway callback', {billId, outcome}); failure logs console.warn('gateway callback rejected', {billId|null, status, errorClass, formEncoded}).

- The audit_log rows gateway_bill.created, gateway_bill.paid and payment.approved were written.
- Collections for 2026-10 now include 627419.

- `createGatewayBill(ctx: ServiceCtx, leaseId: string, asOf: Date = new Date()): Promise<{ billId: string; amountSen: number }>`

- `handleGatewayCallback(rawBody: string, contentType: string | null): Promise<{ status: number; body: unknown }>`
- `signatureSource` and `computeSignature` are also exported for tests.

- **POST /api/leases/[leaseId]/gateway-bills:** 201, 401, 404, 403, 422.
- **GET /api/gateway-bills/[billId]:** 200, 401, 404.

Pending: paid_amount accepts leading zeros ('0627419' = 627419), because the brief's rule is just ^\d+$ plus a safe-integer check.

Pending: paid_at is rewritten as ISO 8601 ('YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM') and parsed with the existing parseInstantWithOffset in dates.ts. That checks the calendar date, hour <= 23, minutes and seconds <= 59, and offset hours <= 23 / minutes <= 59.

Pending: transaction_id and transaction_status are passed to the SQL as-is, or as null when absent, without checking for completed|failed|pending. SPEC says transaction_status is stored but does not drive the state machine.
Pending: the success body is { ok: true, outcome } with outcome 'paid' | 'duplicate' | 'failed' | 'ignored', as the T7 brief says, not the kit's {"duplicate":true}.
Pending: x_signature must be exactly 64 lowercase hex characters (the brief says lowercase hex), so an uppercase-hex signature -> 401.

Pending: a missing or empty GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY -> 500 {error:'Internal error'}, logged as 'gateway key not configured'. The signature-format check runs first, so a callback with a malformed or missing signature still gets 401 when the key is not set.

Pending: logging. The bill id is logged only after the signature is verified and the id is a uuid, so unauthenticated input is never logged. Success logs console.info('gateway callback', {billId, outcome}); failure logs console.warn('gateway callback rejected', {billId|null, status, errorClass, formEncoded}).

Pending: POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills never reads the request body. A same-org staff/manager gets 403: requireLeaseAccess throws its generic 403, and createGatewayBill rethrows it as 403 'Only the lease tenant can pay online'.

Pending: GET /api/gateway-bills/:billId is visible to the bill's lease tenant and to staff/manager of its org (rolesOnLease is not empty); everyone else gets 404 'Bill not found'. The lease lookup is scoped by the bill's own org_id.
findings: Spec conflict, not a code bug: ../SPEC.md Domain rules ('Webhook parsing: ... duplicate keys -> 400') disagrees with the T7 brief ('If any key appears twice -> 401'). I implemented 401 and logged it as D52; SPEC.md should be updated, or the code changed, once the lead decides.
